target: Vi borde planera en gemensam resa tillsammans nästa sommar.
english: We should plan a joint trip together next summer.
grammar: 'Bör/borde' (should/ought to) — 'bör' is present, 'borde' is past/conditional.

target: Hon berörde mig djupt nästa vecka till slut.
english: She touched me deeply next week in the end.

target: De gav oss en fin present till vårt bröllop.
english: They gave us a nice present for our wedding.

target: Måste vi verkligen gå sedan länge alltid?
english: Must we really go for a long time always?

target: Han lärde sig att laga mat under sin tid i Italien.
english: He learned to cook during his time in Italy.

target: De klädde sig fint och åkte till teatern.
english: They dressed up nicely and went to the theater.

target: Kalligrafen övade kinesiska tecken med en tuschpenna.
english: The calligrapher practiced Chinese characters with an ink pen.
grammar: Swedish object pronouns: 'mig' (me), 'dig' (you), 'honom' (him), 'henne' (her), 'oss' (us), 'dem' (them).

target: Ett rikare ordförråd gör det lättare att uttrycka sig.
english: A richer vocabulary makes it easier to express oneself.

target: Inte bara regnade det, det blåste också.
english: Not only did it rain, it was also windy.
grammar: "Inte" goes after the verb in main clauses: "Jag förstår inte" = I don't understand.

target: Han kunde inte sova hela natten på grund av bullret.
english: He couldn't sleep all night because of the noise.

target: De små barnen lekte i trädgården hela eftermiddagen.
english: The small children played in the garden all afternoon.

target: Jag köpte en ny bok i bokhandeln igår.
english: I bought a new book at the bookstore yesterday.

target: Ju längre norrut man åker, desto kallare blir det.
english: The further north you go, the colder it gets.

target: Hennes äldre bror är högre än hennes yngre syster.
english: Her older brother is taller than her younger sister.

target: Det kalla vädret gör att vi stannar hemma hela helgen.
english: The cold weather makes us stay home all weekend.

target: Vi köpte de billigaste biljetterna till den senaste showen.
english: We bought the cheapest tickets to the latest show.

target: Vi letade efter det billigaste flygpriset till Barcelona.
english: We searched for the cheapest flight price to Barcelona.

target: Vi skulle kunna ses på lördag om du har tid då.
english: We could meet on Saturday if you have time then.
grammar: Swedish modal verbs keep the main verb in infinitive at the end: 'Jag kan/vill/ska/måste simma'.

target: Hon sorterar soporna noggrant och återvinner allt hon kan.
english: She sorts the trash carefully and recycles everything she can.
grammar: 'Kan' (can) — doesn't change form. The main verb stays infinitive: 'Jag kan simma' (I can swim).

target: En grön bil stod parkerad utanför vår port hela natten.
english: A green car was parked outside our door all night.

target: En vacker blomma växer i trädgården vid vår stuga.
english: A beautiful flower grows in the garden by our cottage.

target: Jag kan simma i sjön efter en lång arbetsdag.
english: I can swim in the lake after a long workday.

target: Hon köper blommor till sig själv varje fredag som belöning.
english: She buys flowers for herself every Friday as a reward.
grammar: 'Sig' is the reflexive for han/hon/de: 'Han tvättar sig' (He washes himself).

target: De har lärt sig att uppskatta de små sakerna i livet.
english: They have learned to appreciate the small things in life.

target: Vi hade tur att vädret höll sig fint hela dagen.
english: We were lucky that the weather held up all day.

target: Han vill lära sig att spela gitarr efter att ha lyssnat.
english: He wants to learn to play guitar after having listened.

target: Hon använde en vänligare ton när hon talade med barnen.
english: She used a friendlier tone when speaking to the children.

target: De små barnen tycker om att leka i den stora sandlådan.
english: The small children like to play in the big sandbox.

target: Det färska brödet doftade mycket bättre än det gamla.
english: The fresh bread smelled much better than the old one.

target: Ett högt berg syns i fjärran från vårt fönster.
english: A tall mountain is visible in the distance from our window.

target: Parken i vår stadsdel är en perfekt plats att koppla av.
english: The park in our neighborhood is a perfect place to relax.

target: Huset vid stranden är till salu sedan förra månaden.
english: The house by the beach is for sale since last month.

target: Vi ska flytta till en större lägenhet nästa månad.
english: We are going to move to a larger apartment next month.

target: Hon kan baka de godaste kanelbullarna som jag har smakat.
english: She can bake the tastiest cinnamon buns that I have tasted.

target: Han kan laga nästan allting i huset helt på egen hand.
english: He can fix almost everything in the house all by himself.

target: Han skriver dagbok varje kväll innan han går och lägger sig.
english: He writes a diary every evening before he goes to bed.

target: Ett gammalt slott med tjocka murar tornar upp sig i dalen.
english: An old castle with thick walls towers up in the valley.

target: Hon sa ingenting på länge och tittade bara bort.
english: She said nothing for a long time and just looked away.

target: Vi tillbringade en tyst kväll hemma med en bra bok.
english: We spent a quiet evening at home with a good book.

target: En promenad i skogen är det lugnaste jag vet.
english: A walk in the forest is the calmest thing I know.
grammar: Common-gender (en) nouns add '-en' for definite singular: 'en bok' → 'boken'. Neuter (ett) nouns add '-et': 'ett barn' → 'barnet'.

target: En varm sommardag satt vi utomhus och drack kallt vatten.
english: A warm summer day we sat outdoors and drank cold water.

target: Chefen gav er alla en extra ledig dag som bonus.
english: The boss gave you all an extra day off as a bonus.

target: Ett högt torn reser sig över stadens alla gamla hustak.
english: A tall tower rises above all the old rooftops of the city.

target: Det nya biblioteket är större än det förra och modernare.
english: The new library is bigger than the previous one and more modern.

target: De nya reglerna är strängare än de gamla som gällde förut.
english: The new rules are stricter than the old ones that applied before.

target: Han bör söka jobbet innan ansökningstiden går ut på fredag.
english: He should apply for the job before the application period ends on Friday.

target: Vi vill gärna stanna lite längre om det går bra.
english: We would really like to stay a bit longer if that is fine.

target: Jag diskar efter maten sedan länge nästa år.
english: I do the dishes after the meal for a long time next year.
grammar: Swedish object pronouns: 'mig' (me), 'dig' (you), 'honom' (him), 'henne' (her), 'oss' (us), 'dem' (them).

target: Efter en lång arbetsvecka unnade hon sig ett avslappnande bad.
english: After a long week at work, she treated herself to a relaxing bath.

target: Det rena vattnet i sjön är kallare än i havet nu.
english: The clean water in the lake is colder than in the sea now.

target: De mjukaste kuddarna på hotellet finns i sviten på våning tre.
english: The softest pillows at the hotel are in the suite on floor three.

target: Vi behöver en större bil om vi ska åka med alla.
english: We need a bigger car if we are going to go with everyone.

target: Jag tvättar mig.
english: I wash myself.
grammar: Reflexive verbs use "mig/dig/sig/oss/er/sig" — the action reflects back on the subject.

target: Han bryr sig inte.
english: He doesn't care.

target: Det ordnar sig.
english: It will work out.
grammar: Swedes often say "det ordnar sig" to express calm optimism about the future.

target: Han klädde sig fint.
english: He dressed up nicely.

target: Hon bryr sig om oss.
english: She cares about us.

target: Hon klär sig snabbt.
english: She gets dressed quickly.

target: Han skyndar sig till jobbet.
english: He hurries to work.

target: Hon sminkar sig.
english: She puts on makeup.
grammar: Reflexive pronoun "sig" is used for third person: "Han tvättar sig" = He washes himself.

target: Jag tvättar ansiktet.
english: I wash my face.
grammar: Swedish object pronouns: 'mig' (me), 'dig' (you), 'honom' (him), 'henne' (her), 'oss' (us), 'dem' (them).

target: De har inte bestämt sig än.
english: They haven't decided yet.
grammar: "Än" (yet) goes at the end of negative sentences.

target: Hon har lärt sig svenska.
english: She has learned Swedish.

target: De har ännu inte bestämt sig.
english: They still haven't decided.

target: Det regnar inte längre.
english: It's not raining anymore.
grammar: "Inte längre" = no longer / not anymore. "Längre" = longer/anymore.

target: Det är inte mitt fel.
english: It's not my fault.

target: Det är inte sant.
english: It is not true.

target: Det var inte så farligt.
english: It wasn't that bad.

target: Jag vill inte ha något.
english: I don't want anything.

target: Hon har inte ringt ännu.
english: She hasn't called yet.

target: Det löser sig.
english: It will work itself out.

target: Jag vaknar klockan sex.
english: I wake up at six.
grammar: "Vakna" is not reflexive in Swedish, unlike in some other languages.

target: Han tar av sig jackan.
english: He takes off his jacket.

target: Han har bitit sig i tungan.
english: He has bitten his tongue.

target: Kanske kommer han imorgon.
english: Maybe he will come tomorrow.
grammar: "Inte" goes after the verb in main clauses: "Jag förstår inte" = I don't understand.

target: Vi behöver inte stressa.
english: We don't need to stress.

target: Hon behöver inte komma.
english: She doesn't need to come.

target: Jag har inte sett honom.
english: I have not seen him.
grammar: In perfect tense, "inte" goes between "har" and the supine: har + inte + sett.

target: Jag köper aldrig onödiga saker.
english: I never buy unnecessary things.
grammar: Common-gender (en) nouns add '-en' for definite singular: 'en bok' → 'boken'. Neuter (ett) nouns add '-et': 'ett barn' → 'barnet'.

target: Han har aldrig ätit surströmming.
english: He has never eaten surströmming.

target: Vi borde inte ha gjort det.
english: We shouldn't have done it.

target: Vi behöver inte oroa oss.
english: We don't need to worry.
grammar: When you see 'alltid', 'aldrig', or 'ofta' in a Swedish sentence, check if it's a main or subordinate clause to know where to place it.

target: Han trodde inte sina ögon.
english: He didn't believe his eyes.

target: Jag märkte inte skillnaden.
english: I didn't notice the difference.

target: Hon tyckte inte om maten.
english: She didn't like the food.

target: Inte heller jag förstår det.
english: Neither do I understand it.
grammar: "Inte heller" = neither/nor. "Inte heller jag" = me neither.

target: Han pratar i telefon.
english: He talks on the phone.

target: Hon anmäler sig till kursen.
english: She signs up for the course.

target: De slog sig ner vid bordet.
english: They sat down at the table.

target: Hon gifter sig i sommar.
english: She is getting married this summer.

target: Vi myser framför brasan.
english: We cozy up by the fireplace.
grammar: Swedish object pronouns: 'mig' (me), 'dig' (you), 'honom' (him), 'henne' (her), 'oss' (us), 'dem' (them).

target: Han tar av sig skorna inomhus.
english: He takes off his shoes indoors.
grammar: Swedish uses compound words extensively — long words are usually separate words joined together.

target: Jag tvättar mig och klär på mig.
english: I wash up and get dressed.
grammar: Two reflexives in one sentence — each needs its own "mig."

target: Vi förbereder oss för dagen.
english: We prepare ourselves for the day.

target: Hon torkar sig med handduken.
english: She dries herself with the towel.

target: Hon klär på sig vinterjackan.
english: She puts on her winter jacket.

target: Jag undrar om det lönar sig.
english: I wonder if it's worth it.

target: Tusen kronor är inte så mycket.
english: A thousand kronor isn't that much.

target: Vi ska inte stanna länge.
english: We're not going to stay long.
grammar: "Ska inte" = won't / aren't going to. "Länge" = for a long time.

target: Hon har inte alls tid.
english: She has no time at all.
grammar: "Inte alls" = not at all — a common intensifier for negation.

target: Jag vill inte heller gå.
english: I don't want to go either.

target: Vi har sällan tid att vila.
english: We rarely have time to rest.

target: Jag förstår inte vad du menar.
english: I don't understand what you mean.

target: Vi har inte hunnit handla.
english: We haven't had time to shop.

target: Jag tänker inte ge upp.
english: I'm not going to give up.

target: Hon hade inte hunnit äta.
english: She hadn't had time to eat.

target: Tåget stannar inte i Katrineholm.
english: The train doesn't stop in Katrineholm.

target: De har öppnat en ny restaurang.
english: They have opened a new restaurant.

target: Man lär sig så länge man lever.
english: You learn as long as you live.

target: Hellre cyklar jag än kör bil.
english: I'd rather cycle than drive a car.
grammar: In subordinate clauses, "inte" goes before the verb.

target: Det finns ingen hemma just nu.
english: There is nobody home at the moment.
grammar: In main clauses, sentence adverbs (inte, alltid, aldrig, redan) come right after the conjugated verb, not before it.

target: Vi hann inte med tåget.
english: We didn't make it to the train.

target: Han lär sig svenska genom att prata med sina grannar.
english: He learns Swedish by talking with his neighbors.

target: Han ville inte prata om det längre.
english: He didn't want to talk about it anymore.

target: Jag kammar mig framför spegeln.
english: I comb my hair in front of the mirror.
grammar: Daily routine verbs are often reflexive: kammar mig (comb myself), klär mig (dress myself).

target: Jag häller upp ett glas juice till slut.
english: I pour a glass of juice in the end.

target: Nästa vecka börjar den nya kursen på universitetet.
english: Next week the new course at the university begins.
grammar: "Inte" goes after the verb in main clauses: "Jag förstår inte" = I don't understand.

target: Han röker inte längre sedan han slutade förra året.
english: He doesn't smoke anymore since he quit last year.
grammar: "Inte längre" = not anymore / no longer.

target: Om du inte vill, behöver du inte.
english: If you don't want to, you don't have to.

target: Hypotesen kunde inte falsifieras i köket.
english: The hypothesis could not be falsified in the kitchen.
grammar: "Falsifiera" = falsify. "Kunde inte falsifieras" = could not be falsified.

target: De pendlar med tåget till jobbet varje morgon ihop.
english: They commute by train to work every morning together.
grammar: 'Med' (with) — companionship or means: 'med familjen' (with family), 'med tåg' (by train).

target: Hon undervisar barn i engelska på en skola i Malmö.
english: She teaches children English at a school in Malmö.
grammar: Swedish prepositions: 'i' (in), 'på' (on/at), 'till' (to), 'från' (from). Choice depends on context.

target: Vi bor på landet nära en liten by.
english: We live in the countryside near a small village.

target: Hon tänker på sommaren när det är kallt ute.
english: She thinks about summer when it is cold outside.

target: Glada människor samlas i parken varje solig eftermiddag.
english: Happy people gather in the park every sunny afternoon.

target: Rektorn höll ett inspirerande tal vid examensceremonin.
english: The principal gave an inspiring speech at the graduation ceremony.
grammar: "Inspirerande" = inspiring. "Tal" is ett-word: ett tal, talet, tal, talen.

target: Det är spännande att lära sig om andra kulturer och språk.
english: It is exciting to learn about other cultures and languages.

target: Dit vill jag också åka någon gång i framtiden.
english: There I also want to go sometime in the future.
grammar: In subordinate clauses, "inte" goes before the verb.

target: Fiskaren rökte laxen över bokträ hela natten.
english: The fisherman smoked the salmon over beech wood all night.

target: Jag ville inte störa dig så jag väntade utanför.
english: I didn't want to disturb you so I waited outside.

target: En juice till frukost i helgen med familjen.
english: A juice for breakfast on the weekend with the family.

target: Vi har känt varandra sedan vi var små barn.
english: We have known each other since we were small children.
grammar: This sentence uses a group 1 (-ar) verb — the most common verb pattern in Swedish.

target: Ta det lugnt, allt ordnar sig till slut som vanligt.
english: Take it easy, everything works out in the end as usual.

target: Vi fikar med kollegorna klockan tio varje förmiddag på jobbet.
english: We have coffee with colleagues at ten every morning at work.
grammar: 'Med' (with) — companionship or means: 'med familjen' (with family), 'med tåg' (by train).

target: Hon har jobbat som läkare i över femton år nu.
english: She has worked as a doctor for over fifteen years now.

target: De har renoverat hela badrummet med nya kakel och inredning.
english: They have renovated the whole bathroom with new tiles and furnishings.

target: Jag har lagat middag åt familjen varje dag den här veckan.
english: I have cooked dinner for the family every day this week.

target: Hon har hittat en fantastisk ny restaurang nere vid hamnen.
english: She has found a fantastic new restaurant down by the harbor.

target: Boken som jag läser just nu är verkligen väldigt spännande.
english: The book I am reading right now is really very exciting.

target: Utan tvekan är detta den bästa restaurangen i hela staden.
english: Without a doubt this is the best restaurant in the whole city.
grammar: Prepositional phrases count as one unit in first position for V2.

target: Jag tror på dig under den trevliga middagen med alla vännerna.
english: I believe in you during the nice dinner with all the friends.

target: De skrattade åt oss när vi försökte tala svenska i butiken.
english: They laughed at us when we tried to speak Swedish in the store.
grammar: Many Swedish verbs need a preposition with their object: vänta PÅ (wait for).

target: Inte bara blev konserten inställd, utan återbetalningen var också väldigt långsam.
english: Not only was the concert cancelled, but the refund process was also very slow.
grammar: "Inte nog med att" = not only ... (emphatic pattern).

target: Jag kan inte simma.
english: I can't swim.
grammar: "Kan inte" = can't. Negation always after the modal verb in main clauses.

target: Faktiskt tycker jag om vintern.
english: Actually, I like winter.
grammar: "Inte" goes after the verb in main clauses: "Jag förstår inte" = I don't understand.

target: Vi har inte tid.
english: We don't have time.
grammar: When you see 'alltid', 'aldrig', or 'ofta' in a Swedish sentence, check if it's a main or subordinate clause to know where to place it.

target: Jag tycker inte om det.
english: I don't like it.
grammar: "Tycker inte om" = don't like. "Inte" splits "tycker" and "om" (particle).

target: Jag har knappast sovit.
english: I have hardly slept.
grammar: "Knappast" = hardly / barely — a softer negation.

target: Hon gillar inte vinter.
english: She doesn't like winter.
grammar: Swedish double-marks definiteness when using adjectives: 'den stora boken' needs both 'den' and the '-en' suffix.

target: Det spelar inte så stor roll.
english: It doesn't really matter.
grammar: Plural definite forms depend on the declension group: '-na' for most en-words, '-en' or '-a' for ett-words in plural.

target: Han har inte ens försökt.
english: He hasn't even tried.

target: Jag brukar inte klaga.
english: I don't usually complain.

target: Vi ska inte vara oroliga.
english: We shouldn't be worried.

target: Vi handlar på ICA.
english: We shop at ICA.
grammar: ICA is the largest supermarket chain in Sweden.

target: Jag åker med tåg.
english: I go by train.

target: Överallt ser man svenska flaggor.
english: Everywhere you see Swedish flags.
grammar: In subordinate clauses, "inte" goes before the verb.

target: Jag jobbar inte på fredagar.
english: I don't work on Fridays.

target: De har aldrig varit här.
english: They have never been here.

target: Hon tycker inte att det är svårt.
english: She doesn't think it's difficult.

target: Jag har inte träffat henne förut.
english: I haven't met her before.

target: Vi kunde inte hitta vägen.
english: We couldn't find the way.

target: Han ska inte behöva vänta.
english: He shouldn't have to wait.

target: Jag ser inte problemet.
english: I don't see the problem.

target: De kom inte i tid.
english: They didn't arrive on time.

target: Hon väntar på stationen.
english: She waits at the station.

target: Jag studerar på universitetet.
english: I study at the university.

target: De bor nära centrum.
english: They live near the center.
grammar: "Nära" = near. Can be preposition or adverb.

target: Vi ses om en timme.
english: We'll meet in an hour.

target: Hon är bra på svenska.
english: She is good at Swedish.

target: Han skrattar åt skämtet.
english: He laughs at the joke.

target: Jag springer i affären.
english: I run in the store.

target: Januari är den kallaste månaden.
english: January is the coldest month.
grammar: Months are not capitalized in Swedish: januari, februari, mars.

target: Vintern är den kallaste årstiden.
english: Winter is the coldest season.

target: Trots regnet gick vi ut.
english: Despite the rain we went out.

target: I slutändan spelar det ingen roll.
english: In the end it doesn't matter.

target: Nedanför berget ligger en by.
english: Below the mountain lies a village.

target: Vi hade inte tid att vänta.
english: We didn't have time to wait.

target: Jag hoppas att det inte regnar snart.
english: I hope it doesn't rain soon.

target: Jag brukade inte gilla det.
english: I didn't use to like it.

target: Vi kan inte göra något åt det.
english: We can't do anything about it.

target: Det regnade inte trots prognoserna.
english: It didn't rain despite the forecasts.

target: Vi har aldrig haft det här problemet.
english: We have never had this problem.

target: Jag menade inte det så.
english: I didn't mean it that way.

target: Boken ligger i lådan.
english: The book is in the box.

target: Jag är hemma hos min syster.
english: I am at my sister's place.
grammar: "Hemma hos" = at someone's home.

target: Hon väntar vid busshållplatsen.
english: She waits at the bus stop.

target: Sväng till höger vid trafikljuset.
english: Turn right at the traffic light.

target: Sväng till vänster vid nästa korsning.
english: Turn left at the next intersection.
grammar: "Vid" means 'at/by.' Directions: till vänster (left), till höger (right), rakt fram (straight).

target: Hon är äldre än sin bror.
english: She is older than her brother.

target: Det restaurerade slottet väldigt ofta nu.
english: The restored castle very often now.

target: Luciatåget ses i december.
english: The Lucia procession is seen in December.

target: Fortfarande bor hon i samma stad.
english: She still lives in the same city.

target: Under tiden kan du vänta här.
english: In the meantime you can wait here.

target: Nog kan du stanna lite till.
english: Surely you can stay a bit longer.

target: Utomlands fungerar allting lite annorlunda än.
english: Abroad everything works a bit differently than.

target: Jag bor i Sverige vid sjön.
english: I live in Sweden by the lake.

target: Vi kliver av vid nästa station.
english: We get off at the next station.

target: Han är den äldste i familjen.
english: He is the oldest in the family.

target: Vi stänger klockan arton just nu också.
english: We close at eighteen right now too.

target: Ska vi ses imorgon nästa vecka nu?
english: Shall we meet tomorrow next week now?

target: En ny restaurang öppnade nära vårt kontor.
english: A new restaurant opened near our office.
grammar: Frequency adverbs like 'ofta' and 'sällan' sit after the verb in main clauses but before it in subordinate clauses.

target: Framför skolan stannar bussen.
english: In front of the school the bus stops.
grammar: Prepositional phrases count as one unit in first position for V2.

target: Jag kommer hem från jobbet på kvällen.
english: I come home from work in the evening.

target: De köpte ett stort hus nära sjön.
english: They bought a big house near the lake.

target: Den stora bilen stod parkerad utanför affären.
english: The big car was parked outside the store.

target: Jag läste en tjock bok under semestern.
english: I read a thick book during the holiday.

target: En fattig familj fick hjälp av sina grannar.
english: A poor family received help from their neighbors.

target: Det ljusaste rummet i lägenheten ligger mot söder.
english: The brightest room in the apartment faces south.

target: Vi packar lunchlådor just nu under sommaren.
english: We pack lunch boxes right now during summer.

target: Förr eller senare kommer sanningen fram snart.
english: Sooner or later the truth comes out soon.

target: Hantverkaren reparerade takteglet efter stormen.

english: It was much warmer yesterday.

target: Jag bokar biljetten online.
english: I book the ticket online.

target: Pendeltåget går till Södertälje.
english: The commuter train goes to Södertälje.

target: Vi dricker glögg på vintern.
english: We drink mulled wine in winter.
grammar: Glögg is the Swedish mulled wine, spiced and served with almonds and raisins.

target: Vi äter raggmunk med fläsk.
english: We eat potato pancake with pork.

target: Det var den svåraste uppgiften.
english: It was the most difficult task.

target: Det är mindre komplicerat än du tror.
english: It's less complicated than you think.
grammar: "Mindre" = less. "Mindre komplicerat" = less complicated.

target: Vi har väntat i tjugo minuter.
english: We have waited for twenty minutes.

target: Vi har köpt ett nytt hus.
english: We have bought a new house.

target: Han har druckit för mycket kaffe.
english: He has drunk too much coffee.

target: Jag har gått till affären.
english: I have walked to the store.
grammar: "Gå" → "gått" (supine). Irregular.

target: Han har sålt sin gamla bil.
english: He has sold his old car.

target: Jag har talat med chefen.
english: I have spoken with the boss.

target: Vi har dragit i nödtråden.
english: We have pulled the emergency cord.
grammar: Sentence adverbs never appear between the subject and verb in Swedish main clauses — they always follow the conjugated verb.

target: Vi har gått fel.
english: We have gone the wrong way.

target: Jag fyller trettio år imorgon.
english: I turn thirty years old tomorrow.

target: Vi tog tåget till Malmö.
english: We took the train to Malmö.

target: Jag uppskattade henne väldigt ofta nu.
english: I appreciated her very often now.

target: Det är bara tio minuter med tåg.
english: It's only ten minutes by train.

target: Sista bussen gick redan.
english: The last bus has already left.

target: Det framkom att ingen visste.
english: It turned out that nobody knew.
grammar: Place 'inte' (not) directly after the verb in main clauses: 'Jag äter inte' — but in subclauses it moves before the verb.

target: Fyll på glaset just nu nog!
english: Refill the glass right now probably!

target: Seglaren navigerade genom det stormiga sundet.
english: The sailor navigated through the stormy strait.
grammar: Swedish object pronouns: 'mig' (me), 'dig' (you), 'honom' (him), 'henne' (her), 'oss' (us), 'dem' (them).

target: Vi har alltid pepparkakor till jul.
english: We always have gingerbread cookies for Christmas.

target: Tåget är försenat med tio minuter.
english: The train is delayed by ten minutes.
grammar: The adverb position flips between main and subordinate clauses: 'Jag dricker aldrig...' vs. 'att jag aldrig dricker...'

target: Det händer att bussen är sen.
english: It happens that the bus is late.
grammar: When you see 'alltid', 'aldrig', or 'ofta' in a Swedish sentence, check if it's a main or subordinate clause to know where to place it.

target: Ännu idag minns jag den kvällen verkligen.
english: Even today I remember that evening really.
grammar: Remember: 'inte' after the verb in main clauses ('Han köper inte'), but before in subclauses ('att han inte köper').

target: Ge inte upp på morgonen nu!
english: Don't give up in the morning now!

target: Njut av resan efter jobbet just nu!
english: Enjoy the trip after work right now!
grammar: Swedish definite nouns look different from English 'the': the article is fused onto the end, making Swedish nouns longer in definite form.

target: Beställ vad du vill nästa vecka nu!
english: Order whatever you want next week now!
grammar: The BIFF rule (Bisats Inte Före Finita verbet) helps remember: in subclauses, 'inte' comes before the finite verb.

target: De diskuterar politik vid middagsbordet nästan.
english: They discuss politics at the dinner table almost.

target: Hon ställde en viktig fråga under mötet.
english: She asked an important question during the meeting.

target: Hon skrev adressen på ett tunt papper.
english: She wrote the address on a thin paper.

target: Han hängde en ren skjorta i garderoben.
english: He hung a clean shirt in the wardrobe.

target: Vi har alltid ett rent kök hemma.
english: We always keep a clean kitchen at home.

target: Jag vill ha lite grädde till kaffet.
english: I would like some cream for the coffee.

target: En flaska mineralvatten, tack ibland snart.
english: A bottle of mineral water, please sometimes soon.

target: Vi hyrer en elsparkcykel väldigt ofta nu.
english: We rent an electric scooter very often now.

target: Meteorologen förutsåg kraftigt snöfall i norr.
english: The meteorologist predicted heavy snowfall in the north.
grammar: Swedish adverb placement is tied to clause type — after the verb in main clauses, before it in subclauses starting with att/som/när.

target: Ring mig imorgon på kvällen för alla!
english: Call me tomorrow in the evening for everyone!

target: Plocka upp efter dig på morgonen nu!
english: Pick up after yourself in the morning now!

target: Lantmätaren markerade tomtgränsen med röda pinnar.
english: The surveyor marked the property boundary with red stakes.
grammar: Object pronouns: mig (me), dig (you), honom (him), henne (her), oss (us), er (you pl.), dem (them).

target: Diakonissan hjälpte de hemlösa med mat och kläder.
english: The deaconess helped the homeless with food and clothing.

target: Det var den roligaste filmen jag någonsin har sett.
english: That was the funniest movie I have ever seen.

target: Vi måste fatta ett viktigt beslut före fredag.
english: We have to make an important decision before Friday.

target: Vi gick längs en bred gata kantad med träd.
english: We walked along a wide street lined with trees.

target: Den tystaste platsen i huset är vinden.
english: The quietest place in the house is the attic.
grammar: Plural definite forms depend on the declension group: '-na' for most en-words, '-en' or '-a' for ett-words in plural.

target: Det var en blöt dag så vi stannade inomhus.
english: It was a wet day so we stayed indoors.

target: Hon är den smartaste personen jag någonsin har träffat.
english: She is the smartest person I have ever met.

target: En svensk tradition är att fira midsommar med sill.
english: A Swedish tradition is to celebrate midsummer with herring.

target: Det smalaste stråket av kusten har de brantaste klipporna.
english: The narrowest stretch of coast has the steepest cliffs.

target: Hon köpte den mjukaste filten och det tjockaste täcket.
english: She bought the softest blanket and the thickest duvet.

target: De hårdaste vintrarna gör oss starkare och mer tåliga.
english: The harshest winters make us stronger and more resilient.

target: Vi har planerat en stor fest till nästa helg.
english: We have planned a big party for next weekend.
grammar: Group 1 supine: -at ending: 'har arbetat' (has worked), 'har pratat' (has talked).

target: Välkommen hem igen, vi har saknat dig jättemycket.
english: Welcome home again, we have missed you very much.
grammar: Group 1 supine: -at ending: 'har arbetat' (has worked), 'har pratat' (has talked).

target: Jag har stått i kö i en timme.
english: I have been standing in line for an hour.

target: Hon har jobbat som lärare sedan hon tog examen.
english: She has worked as a teacher since she graduated.

target: Vi har tagit emot många ansökningar till den nya tjänsten.
english: We have received many applications for the new position.

target: Jag ser fram emot att träffa hela din familj snart.
english: I look forward to meeting your whole family soon.
grammar: 'Snart' (soon) — 'Vi ska snart gå' (We will soon go).

target: Redan klockan sex vaknade jag ibland också.
english: Already at six o'clock I woke up sometimes too.
grammar: "Redan" = already. When fronted, V2 rule applies.

target: Hon vann tävlingen och alla gratulerade henne efteråt.
english: She won the competition and everyone congratulated her afterwards.

target: Vi får inte underskatta svårigheterna ibland nästa år.
english: We must not underestimate the difficulties sometimes next year.

target: Var snäll och stäng av telefonen under hela föreställningen.
english: Please turn off the phone during the entire performance.

target: En kall vind blåste in genom det öppna fönstret ikväll.
english: A cold wind blew in through the open window tonight.

target: Ett moln dolde solen och det blev plötsligt kallt.
english: A cloud hid the sun and it suddenly became cold.

target: Selma Lagerlöf var den första kvinnliga Nobelpristagaren i litteratur.
english: Selma Lagerlöf was the first female Nobel laureate in literature.

target: Hon är lång och syns alltid i en folksamling.
english: She is tall and always stands out in a crowd.
grammar: "Lång" = tall/long. Comparative: längre. Superlative: längst.

target: Det är den vackraste platsen jag någonsin har besökt.
english: That is the most beautiful place I have ever visited.

target: En hög byggnad stod i slutet av gatan.
english: A tall building stood at the end of the street.

target: Det var den mest spännande filmen jag någonsin sett.
english: That was the most exciting movie I have ever seen.

target: Den varmaste dagen i år var den tjugonde juli faktiskt.
english: The warmest day this year was the twentieth of July.

target: Den grå katten är mycket lugnare än den svarta valpen.
english: The gray cat is much calmer than the black puppy.

target: Det bredaste leendet jag har sett tillhör min dotter.
english: The broadest smile I have seen belongs to my daughter.

target: Det djupaste havet utanför kusten lockar många erfarna dykare.
english: The deepest sea off the coast attracts many experienced divers.

target: Jag har hört att du talar flera olika språk flytande.
english: I have heard that you speak several different languages fluently.
grammar: Group 2/3 supine: -t ending: 'har köpt' (has bought), 'har bott' (has lived).

target: Han har sprungit maraton tre gånger de senaste åren.
english: He has run a marathon three times in recent years.

target: Han har studerat medicin i sex år vid Karolinska institutet.
english: He has studied medicine for six years at Karolinska Institute.

target: Jag har försökt ringa henne flera gånger utan att lyckas.
english: I have tried to call her several times without succeeding.

target: Hon har dansat balett sedan barndomen och älskar det fortfarande.
english: She has danced ballet since childhood and still loves it.

target: Han har spelat fotboll sedan han var sex år gammal.
english: He has played football since he was six years old.

target: Han har fotograferat fåglar i naturen sedan han var ung.
english: He has photographed birds in nature since he was young.

target: Vi har äntligen hittat en pålitlig hantverkare till renoveringen.
english: We have finally found a reliable craftsman for the renovation.

target: Hon har läst om svensk historia och blivit väldigt intresserad.
english: She has read about Swedish history and become very interested.

target: De har ordnat en överraskningsfest till hans femtionde födelsedag.
english: They have arranged a surprise party for his fiftieth birthday.

target: Tack så mycket för hjälpen, det var snällt.
english: Thank you so much for the help, that was kind.
grammar: This is the standard phrase when meeting someone for the first time.
